clue.text: Takes short trips, full of energy and aspirations

indicators.note: the trips word is filled with the energy letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to hop is to make a short journey, so takes short trips = hops
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone flitting about on brief journeys, buzzing with energy and ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonym: aspirations are things one longs for, the same as wishes or ambitions.

clue.text: Leaders not quite what the Queen of Hearts ordered, say?

indicators.note: not quite means the phrase stops one letter short of its full form

parts.words: what the Queen of Hearts ordered
parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Queen of Hearts keeps shouting 'Off with their heads!', i.e. heads off
to say is to state

explanation.surface: A mock-literary aside about rulers and the Queen of Hearts' famous decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the last F from HEADS OFF, leaving HEADS OF; 'say' then supplies STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Presidents and monarchs are national figureheads, so the plural phrase means leaders of countries.

clue.text: Drive first person boarding cleaner, low-level transport

parts.note: to drive something forward is to push it

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the person letter goes inside the cleaner word

parts.note: a char is a British word for a cleaning lady
I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A cleaner pushing a trolley about on her rounds, with a passenger aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is British slang for a cleaning woman (charwoman).
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's buggy sits close to the ground, so it is a humorous description of a low-slung vehicle.

clue.text: Lecher lines up at end of day

indicators.note: at end of places the lines word after the day word

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the lines word is written backwards

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. lines

explanation.surface: A womaniser lining up at the end of the day, perhaps at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway) reversed by 'up' gives YR.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the goat-legged woodland god is a byword for lust, so it names a lustful man.

clue.text: Stop cricket side going on holiday

indicators.note: going on puts the cricket side after the holiday word

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team heading off on holiday together.
explanation.walkthrough: The OFF side in cricket is the half of the field the batsman faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal-verb synonym: to cease doing something, as in 'leave off nagging'.

clue.text: Smallest member in Oxford, possibly?

parts.note: an Oxford is a type of laced shoe, and the smallest digit of the foot sits inside it

explanation.surface: The most junior fellow of an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a club or college; it is a body part, and an Oxford is a lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth digit of the foot is the tiniest limb-end and lives inside a shoe.

clue.text: International alliance putting a boundary up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the boundary word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: in cricket a boundary hit over the rope scores six

explanation.surface: Nations forming a pact and pushing out their frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball struck over the boundary rope without bouncing scores six; 'up' turns that word upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical example: Germany, Italy and Japan formed the wartime alliance known by this name.

clue.text: Instrument you fake for listeners? I'm not sure

indicators.note: for listeners means the words are to be heard, not read

parts.note: you phoney, said aloud
um is a hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone accused of faking it on an instrument, who answers hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you phoney' heard gives EUPHONI-; UM is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tenor brass instrument of the tuba family, common in brass bands.

clue.text: Dodgy handler, one of many at Aintree?

definitions.meaning: a receiver of stolen goods is called a ...
Aintree racecourse hosts the Grand National, a steeplechase over many jumps

explanation.surface: A shady character among the crowds at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse of the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a dealer in stolen goods, and the obstacle horses jump in a steeplechase.

clue.text: Like groups on vacation, getting money by selling things off

definitions.text: getting money by selling things off

parts.note: as means like
sets are groups
tripping means going on trips, on holiday

explanation.surface: Holiday parties raising cash by flogging their possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Business term for buying a company and selling off its assets piecemeal for profit.

clue.text: Routine problem for emerging divers lacking second potty

parts.note: a round is a routine of regular duties

indicators.note: lacking means the second's letter is taken out of the divers' problem

parts.note: decompression sickness, suffered by divers surfacing too fast, is the bends

explanation.surface: A diver's routine, the hazard of surfacing, and a missing second.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang synonym for mad: both mean crazy.

clue.text: Fast no doubt broken by backsliding church

indicators.note: broken by means the doubt-free word is split with the church letters inside

parts.note: surely means without doubt

indicators.note: backsliding means the church letters run backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A firm belief shaken by a church slipping back into old ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' means firmly fixed here, not quick; CE reversed gives EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb sense: held fast means held firmly, tightly fixed.

clue.text: Dance, or eastern ball of sorts, going west

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading right to left

parts.note: a lob is a kind of high ball in tennis or cricket

explanation.surface: A choice between dancing or a ball held somewhere in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, E and LOB together reversed give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Spanish dance in triple time, made famous by Ravel.

clue.text: Revived fur trade's criminal

indicators.note: revived means brought back in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The fur trade, reborn, is a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a cheat or swindler is a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Provincial county short of land for deportees at one time?

definitions.text: land for deportees at one time?

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland, often called the Province
under means less than, short of

explanation.surface: An Irish county short of land for transportation.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland, which the British call 'the Province'.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia, nickname for the land where Britain shipped convicts in the 18th and 19th centuries.

clue.text: Redundant staff are often kept on, Republican admitted

indicators.note: admitted means the Republican letter is let inside the kept word

parts.note: retained means kept on

explanation.surface: Staff laid off, some kept on, a Republican let in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the sentence to complete: redundant staff are often ____.
explanation.definitionFit: Completing the sentence: workers laid off are commonly taught new skills for fresh jobs.

clue.text: Revolutionary children's writer having no time for dramatist

indicators.note: having no means the time letter is dropped
revolutionary means turned round, so the writer's name runs backwards

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A rebellious author for the young who had no time for a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: NESBIT reversed is TIBSEN; dropping T leaves the Norwegian playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Henrik, the Norwegian author of A Doll's House, is a celebrated playwright.

clue.text: Brown junior soundly beaten?

indicators.note: soundly signals the junior word is taken as heard

parts.note: a son is a junior
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: A boy given a sound thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like an intensifier for beaten; it signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: skin darkened by the sun is bronzed.

clue.text: Cast leading pair in third series

indicators.note: leading pair in picks the first two letters of the next word

parts.note: a row is a series of things in a line

explanation.surface: A cast list headed by two stars in the third series of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests actors; here it is the verb to fling.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to cast a stone is to hurl or fling it.

clue.text: Nutmeg's in tiddly state in a small cafe

indicators.note: in means the setter's possessive sits inside the jumbled letters
tiddly means slightly drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: Nutmeg is the setter, so Nutmeg's means mine

explanation.surface: The setter tipsy in a little cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: ESTAT (from 'state', mixed by 'tiddly') takes MINE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loanword for a small bar or bistro selling drinks and simple food.

clue.text: Small vessel raised after master abandons her

indicators.note: after places the raised word behind the shortened master word
abandons means the word her is dropped

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
up means raised

explanation.surface: A cup lifted after a schoolmaster walks out on his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: TEACHER without HER leaves TEAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup for drinking is a little container, i.e. a small vessel.

clue.text: Gnome's promotion coming with maturity

parts.note: an ad promotes a product
age means maturity

explanation.surface: A garden gnome promoted as it matures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' is not the garden figure: it is a pithy saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare sense: a gnome is a maxim or aphorism, a short wise saying.

clue.text: Consider introducing collars round poisonous plant

indicators.note: introducing means the consider word takes the collars word inside

parts.note: to rate is to consider, as in rate highly

indicators.note: round means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: nabs means collars, i.e. arrests

explanation.surface: Arresting someone who sits beside a toxic plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collars' is slang for arrests, not neckwear; 'round' turns it back before 'introducing' sets it inside the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A name for various toxic plants, or rat poison, whose name means 'bane of rats'.

clue.text: What those waiting do to start play?

definitions.meaning: waiters wait on diners, bringing them food
in tennis a point begins with the ... first shot

explanation.surface: Players waiting their turn to begin a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiting' means waiting at table.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb with two senses: to dish food to diners, and to strike the opening shot in tennis.

clue.text: Available payment about right

indicators.note: about means the payment word goes round the right letter

parts.note: a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: A fee on offer that seems fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unoccupied or not busy, as in 'Are you free on Tuesday?'

clue.text: Romanian garden yielding fruit

indicators.note: yielding means the garden's letters give up a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Romanian garden producing its crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small loose-skinned citrus, a kind of tangerine.

clue.text: Look out for GI avoiding complex debriefing

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier ducking out of a tricky debrief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' and 'complex' together signal a composite anagram: the soldier's two letters are subtracted from the briefing word's pool before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to befriend someone is to take them under your wing and help them.

clue.text: Put paid to journalists concealing name

indicators.note: concealing means the journalists hide the name letter inside

parts.note: ED is short for editor, so two eds make journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters hiding a name, finishing off a story.
explanation.walkthrough: Two EDs (editors) are the journalists, with N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to put paid to something is to finish it off, bring it to a close.
